metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets Singapore

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 creative thinking results for Singapore using the OECD PISA 2022 Database. The document does not specify the exact student sampling weight variable name or whether replicate weights were used, but PISA results are produced under a complex two-stage sampling design (schools, then students) and are typically analyzed with sampling weights to obtain population-representative estimates. The factsheet also reports uncertainty intervals (95% confidence intervals) and notes about sampling standards not being met for some countries/economies, indicating that the OECD’s standard PISA variance estimation approach was applied. No additional preprocessing or analytic subsampling rules are described beyond the Singapore-specific reporting and the use of PISA creative thinking scales and related background measures.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a country factsheet summarizing published PISA 2022 results rather than an empirical study that models student-level cognitive outcomes with an explicitly stated PV-based analysis pipeline. The factsheet reports scale scores, proficiency levels, and associations (e.g., variance explained) using OECD’s already-produced PISA estimates, but it does not describe how plausible values or missing data were handled in the underlying estimation. Therefore, PV and missing-data handling details are not available from the provided text.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used the Singapore analytic sample of 15-year-old students who completed the PISA 2022 assessment in mathematics, reading, or science and for whom creative thinking results are reported in the PISA 2022 Volume III creative thinking factsheet. The factsheet does not describe additional exclusions (e.g., missing background questionnaire items) or task-level completion filters beyond the stated completion of the assessment and the OECD’s standard PISA data quality/sampling standards.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III factsheet reports Singapore’s performance on the PISA 2022 Creative Thinking cognitive test for 15-year-old students. The creative thinking assessment measures how students generate diverse and creative ideas and how they evaluate and improve others’ ideas, using 32 open-ended tasks scored via human judgement and detailed rubrics. Results are reported on a 60-point scale and also mapped to proficiency levels (e.g., baseline Level 3 and top levels 5–6). For Singapore, the mean creative thinking score is 41 (OECD average 33), and 94% of students reach at least Level 3, while 58% are top performers (Level 5 or 6). The factsheet also reports within-Singapore performance gaps by socio-economic status and gender, and provides associations between creative thinking and mathematics/reading performance, including the share of variance in creative thinking uniquely attributed to mathematics performance.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a descriptive OECD factsheet summarizing already-estimated PISA 2022 creative thinking results for Singapore, not an original empirical paper that trains or evaluates machine learning models. As a result, there is no student-level ML modelling pipeline, no explicit PV-handling or missing-data strategy described in the text, and no reported ML performance metrics to populate main_findings. The extraction therefore focuses on the assessment design and reported benchmarks rather than predictive modelling outputs.
